title: [M-06] Recovery can be done without Guardians’ approvals by looking at initial account update tx data
description:
lib/src/account/v0.rs [# L436](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L436)

In general, recovery can only be done with Guardians’ approvals, since we need to [recover](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L327-L333) secret from guardians’ shares and use secret + msk_ss_rik to [calculate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L336) key_data, which will then be used to [decrypt the original data](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L339) (in social recovery, data is msk_ss_social).

However, when an account is initially registered, AccountUpdate struct’s social recovery information is unsafely generated with [weak parameters (threshold = 0)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L409-L416). This allows derivation of key_data and key_meta without relying on guardian shares.

AccountUpdate of initial account registration is registered on chain and publicly available. So anyone with msk_ss_rik can look up transaction history and can decrypt original data (msk_ss_social) without possession of guardian shares, because key_data and key_meta of the initial social recovery can be calculated deterministically.

With msk_ss_rik and msk_ss_social, one can [derive](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L694-L698) msk_decryption_key and recover account’s msk from AccountState.rec.enc_msk

This is a violation of one of the main invariants:

Recovery of a backup only occurs when more than the specified threshold of Guardians has approved the request.

Finding description and impact

The root cause stems from the following facts:

When account secret is generated, recovery.social is created with default parameters (guardians = [], threshold = 0) [trace1](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L409-L416), [trace2](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L436)

File: lib/src/account/v0.rs

​
   409:         let social = create_recovery(
   410:             rng, //
   411:             acc,
   412:             &msk_ss_rik,
   413:             &msk_ss_social,
   414:@>           &[],
   415:@>           0,
   416:         )?;
   

This allows deterministic derivation of key_meta and key_data without relying on guardians’ shares

sss::share will return (Fr::ZERO, []) for threshold 0 [trace1](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L380), [trace2](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/crypto/sss.rs# L38-L40)

File: lib/src/backup/v0.rs

​
      // @audit threshold = 0, guardians = []
      380: let (secret, shares) = sss::share(rng, threshold, guardians.len());
      
  File: lib/src/crypto/sss.rs

​
      32: pub(crate) fn share<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
      33:     rng: &mut R,
      34:     t: usize,
      35:     n: usize,
      36: ) -> (Secret, Vec<Share>) {
      37:     // a threshold 0 sharing is just a constant
      38:     if t == 0 {
      39:@>       return (Secret(pp::Fr::ZERO), vec![]);
      40:     }
      

As a result, key_meta and key_data can be directly calculated from msk_ss_rik

key_meta = kdfn(msk_ss_rik, "KDFMetakey" || [])

[File: lib/src/backup/v0.rs](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L404)

​
         // @audit comms = []
         404: let key_meta: [u8; sym::SIZE_KEY] = kdfn(sym_key, &KDFMetakey { comms: &comms });
         
  2. `key_data = kdfn("BackupKDFInput" || msk_ss_rik || Fr::ZERO, "EmptyInfo")`

     [File: lib/src/backup/v0.rs](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L409-L415)

​
         409: let key_data: [u8; sym::SIZE_KEY] = kdfn(
         410:             &BackupKDFInput {
         411:                 key: sym_key,
         412:                 secret, // @audit secret = 0
         413:             },
         414:             &EmptyInfo,
         415:         );
         

This recovery.social information is available on chain because it’s included in initial account update transaction [trace1](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L635-L724), [trace2](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L703-L717)

File: lib/src/account/v0.rs

   635:     pub fn update<R: Rng + CryptoRng>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> Result<AccountUpdate> {
   ...
   703:         let st = AccountStateV0 {
   ...
   710:             rec: RecoveryStateV0 {
   711:                 pke: None,
   712:                 assoc,
   713:                 // TODO: unfortunately we cannot generate this anew every time
   714:@>               social: self.recovery.social.clone(),
   715:                 enc_msk,
   716:             },
   717:         };
   718:
   719:         let sig = self.old_sig.sign(rng, &st);
   720:         Ok(AccountUpdate::V0(AccountUpdateV0 {
   721:             acc: self.acc,
   722:@>           msg: AccountMessageV0::Update(AccountUpdateFullV0 { sig, state: st }),
   723:         }))
   

This means anyone with the knowledge of msk_ss_rik can recover msk_ss_social because:
4. Since initial account_update.rec.social is visible on chain, social recovery BackupCipherText is known
5. This initial recovery is generated with known parameters i.e. threshold = 0, guardians = []
6. BackupCipherText is comprised of the following values [ref](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L61-L65):

data = Sym.Seal(key_meta, BackupMetadata(Sym.Seal(key_data, msk_ss_social))) [ref](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L420-L432)

encap = [] because threshold = 0

comms = [] due to the same reason

Since key_data and key_meta can be calculated from msk_ss_rik, msk_ss_social can be decrypted from BackupCipherText

With msk_ss_rik and msk_ss_social, one can [derive](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L694-L698) msk_decryption_key and recover account’s msk.

Impact

This is a violation of one of the main invariants in the README:

Recovery of a backup only occurs when more than the specified threshold of Guardians has approved the request.

FAQ

Q: This attack requires the knowledge of msk_ss_rik, which is a significant restriction.

A: Correct, however I believe this report is worth Medium severity because it violates the main invariant. Without the invariant, I wouldn’t have submitted this issue. Moreover, key_data and key_meta should be only retrieved from guardians’ approval, even for the party that knows msk_ss_rik. That’s because guardians “guard” [secret](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L380), from which key_data is [derived](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/backup/v0.rs# L409-L415). However, the protocol publicly shares unsafe encryption of msk_ss_social by mistake.

Q: How do you know initial account update will always contain unsafe social recovery?

A: Because AccountUpdate.msg.state.rec.social property is mandatory and will be very likely to be filled with the explained [library logic](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L397)

[AccountUpdate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/contracts/src/lib.rs# L114) -> [AccountUpdateV0](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/mod.rs# L68) -> [AccountMessageV0](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L34) -> [AccountUpdateFullV0](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L295) -> [AccountStateV0](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L302) -> [RecoveryStateV0](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L233) -> [social: BackupCipherText](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L104)

File: lib/src/account/v0.rs

​
101: pub(crate) struct RecoveryStateV0 {
102:     pub pke: Option<pke::EncryptionKey>, // this is set iff. recovery has been started
103:     pub(crate) assoc: Vec<AssociationsV0>, // encryption of the recovery authorization key
104:@>   pub(crate) social: BackupCiphertext, // social backup ciphertext
105:     pub(crate) enc_msk: sym::AEADCiphertext, // encrypted MSK (encrypted with key derived from RIK and social shares)
106: }

Q: This only happens for account that did not initiate social recovery. If the account initiates a social recovery, rec.social will be updated with BackupCipherText generated with non-zero threshold and guardians.

A: Wrong. Accounts that initiated social recovery are also affected by this issue. Although new rec.social will be much more secure with non-zero threshold, initial account update transaction and account_update information is still visible on chain. Anyone with msk_ss_rik can recover initial msk_ss_social by looking at initial account update string. And with msk_ss_rik and the initial msk_ss_social, they can recover account’s msk. This breaks the main invariant.

Q: This report is wrong because msk_ss_social is [rotated](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L542) on recovery initiation. So even if you decrypted old mks_ss_social, it’s outdated and useless.

A: Nope, the main impact of this issue is msk recover without guardians’ approval, and we can decrypt msk from old msk_ss_social and old enc_msk, recorded on initial account update. More specifically, during account initialization, AccountUpdate [contains](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L105) msg.state.rec.enc_msk, which is generated as Sym.Seal(kdfn(msk_ss_rik, msk_ss_social_old), msk) [ref](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-11-swafe/blob/15056ba589b62c52cd4530a78cc5c0be22682e56/lib/src/account/v0.rs# L692-L701). Since msk_ss_rik does not change, we can decrypt msk from enc_msk_old with msk_ss_rik and msk_ss_social_old.

Recommended mitigation steps

Don’t generate initial social recovery with trivial parameters.

Make social property optional and fill it only when recovery is initiated.

[Swafe mitigated](https://github.com/code-423n4/2026-03-swafe-mitigation?tab=readme-ov-file# mitigation-of-high--medium-severity-issues):

Set threshold=1 in gen() so initial recovery backup is unrecoverable (0 shares < threshold 1)

Move guardians.len() < threshold check from BackupCiphertextV0::new to public backup() API, allowing internal create_recovery() to produce intentionally unrecoverable backups

Status: Mitigation confirmed. Full details in reports from montecristo, niffylord, and DCENT09.
